units.coordinate: q is logarithmic radial scale and is treated as dimensionless
units.operators: D=partial_q and C=partial_q^2-1/4 are dimensionless in this normalization
units.graph_metric: ||f||^2+||Cf||^2 fixes the relative coefficient of two equivalent graph norms to one; changing that coefficient changes the numerical contraction bound

interior_constant.spectral_variable: lambda>=0 is the eigenvalue of D^*D
interior_constant.number_theory: 17=16+1 comes only from the unit graph term and the fourth power of the half-density mass; 8 appears after algebraic simplification

boundary_constant.chosen_lift: R_1(a,b)=a exp(q) on q<0 and b exp(-q) on q>0
boundary_constant.origin: the 3-4-5 triangle is arithmetic from rates 1 and 3/4

general_lift.family: R_kappa uses exp(kappa q) on the left and exp(-kappa q) on the right, kappa>0
general_lift.consequence: 4/5 is specific to kappa=1, chosen because it is a convenient norm-one H1 trace lift; it is not intrinsic to the boundary quotient

categorical_nonrelation.C4: no relation is established between 4/5 and the order-four Fourier/Clifford cycle
categorical_nonrelation.simplex: 17, 8, 4, and 5 do not count simplex faces or coherence dimensions
categorical_nonrelation.test: rescaling the graph metric or choosing another Poisson right inverse changes the constants while leaving all C4 and simplicial identities unchanged

correct_claim_boundary: These calculations prove that particular normalized incidence operators are strict contractions in particular graph norms. They do not supply a source-invariant Birman-Schwinger chamber margin until the exact Green metric and canonical Poisson normalization are fixed by the source construction.
conclusion: The apparent powers of two are algebraic consequences of the half-density mass 1/2 and unit graph-norm coefficient. The 4/5 is a 3-4-5 normalization arising from the convenient exponential lift of rate one. Neither number currently has simplex or C4 significance.
